correctness.rationale: The gamma representation gives a positive Gram operator with finite sum of diagonal entries for beta>1. For an independent normalization check set beta=1+epsilon and sum the positive entry products under the three gamma integrals. The three resulting factors are zeta(1+t_i+t_j). With R=sum t_i and u_i=t_i/R, the integral over R<1 is Gamma(1+epsilon)^(-3) times the integral of R^(-1+3epsilon) times the simplex weight product(u_i^epsilon/(1-u_i)), up to a uniformly integrable remainder. Indeed 1/s <= zeta(1+s) <= 1+1/s by integral comparison, so replacing the zeta factors by their poles, and e^(-R) by 1, incurs a relative O(R) error uniformly on the simplex. For R>=1 the exponential and the integrable weight product(1-u_i)^(-1) give a uniform bound. Dominated convergence for the angular weight (one inverse linear singularity per vertex in two variables) and the radial integral 1/(3epsilon) yield A/3. At fixed t=u_1+u_2, partial fractions give A=integral_0^1 [-2 log(1-t)/(t(2-t))] dt. Setting t=1-exp(-v), then expanding 1/sinh(v), gives A=2 sum_{j>=0}(2j+1)^(-2)=pi^2/4. This confirms pi^2/12. The published proof's log quadrature also checks: every proper face has integrable decay at beta=1, and the angular majorant for the radial Abel limit is integrable. The first- and second-moment checks follow from integrating (1+2x)^(-beta) and R(1+R)^(-2beta), respectively; both quadrature errors are bounded as beta decreases to 1.
correctness.reproducibility: Inspected VERIFICATION.md and CHECK.py without running the uploaded script. Independent composite Simpson quadrature of v/sinh(v), with the value 1 at zero, 24,000 equal panels on [0,30], gives 2.4674011002665 (pi^2/4 is 2.4674011002723); the omitted tail is at most 2(30+1)exp(-30)/(1-exp(-60)). This checks only the angular coefficient numerically. The analytic argument supplies the limit. The frozen expert, independent-audit, and Lean channels report not_performed.

value.rationale: The parameter is the trace-class threshold of an existing natural Helson family. The first two residues are both 1/2; they do not determine the cubic singularity. The cubic residue identifies the first genuine three-variable contribution and gives a concrete test value for any proposed critical trace distribution or comparison with the Carleman model. The exact number and effective length matter here, rather than a numerical estimate for an arbitrarily selected parameter.
